children: Global metals are facing selling pressure all through this week so far. Silver is leading the decline down 8%, followed by gold at 4.5%, copper at 4%, and aluminium at 3%. Bucking the broader downward trend, alumina prices have surged to $390 per tonne, adding to margin pressure for non-integrated producers.

The sell-off is being driven by a confluence of macroeconomic headwinds and shifting demand expectations. Investors are factoring in a potential slowdown in AI-related capital expenditure alongside persistent inflationary pressures and rising bond yields. These dynamics have pushed the US Dollar index to a 19-month high, with markets now pricing in a greater than 90% probability of a Federal Reserve rate hike in December 2026.

For aluminium specifically, fundamental headwinds are also mounting. According to Axis Capital, global demand growth slowed to 1.2% year-on-year during the first nine months of 2026, a noticeable deceleration from the 3% compound annual growth rate (CAGR) recorded between 2023 and 2025. Furthermore, the global aluminium market is projected to swing into a surplus of 0.5 million tonnes per annum (MTPA) in 2027, capping near-term upside.

In contrast, domestic steelmakers appear better insulated from global volatility. Pricing in the steel sector remains largely domestic in nature, supported by safeguard duties that protect local producers from cheap imports. With underlying demand improving, the sector is positioned for strong volume growth in the second half of FY27. Supporting this view, HSBC notes that domestic steel prices are currently trading at a 5% to 6% premium over imported Chinese steel.

The Nifty Metal index is the top sectoral loser on Wednesday, with shares of Vedanta Aluminium and Steel Authority of India (SAIL) emerging as the top two losers on the index, with declines of 5.5% each.
Shares of NALCO and Hindustan Zinc fell over 4% each, as did shares of Vedanta Ltd. Jindal Steel, Hindustan Copper and Hindalco saw losses of close to 3% on Wednesday.

title: Metal Stocks Under Pressure: Why Domestic Steel Outshines Aluminium Amid Global Sell-Off
